newsitem.title: BELGIUM: France to insist modified maize is labelled.
newsitem.headline: France to insist modified maize is labelled.

text.p: The French government has been notified of the European Commission's decision that genetically modified maize is safe, but will delay its release on the market until labelling conditions are met.
"The Commission notified the French government on January 24 of its decision in December that modified maize was safe.
"Authorisation of modified maize for the European Union market will depend on an obligatory condition that animal feed made with the product is labelled," a French diplomat said on Wednesday.
The French government accepts that producers and traders have said they will adopt a voluntary labelling code of practice but will insist on a compulsory system, the diplomat added.
"The government is studying ways of ensuring that consumer information is carried on products containing modified maize and we want to see a directive at European level," he said.
French farm minister Philippe Vasseur said last month that genetically modified maize, developed by Swiss firm Ciba-Geigy, would not be authorised on the EU market until labelling laws were in place.

French customs earlier this month seized several shipments of modified maize arriving at French ports from the U.S., which said that a refusal to authorise their modified maize would have serious trade implications.
Under EU rules, France has to authorise the placing of genetically modified maize on the market before any other country can do so because it was the member state which asked for permission to do so.
"The matter is now out of the Commission's hands. The Commission decided that genetically modified maize could safely be allowed on the EU market after taking scientific advice.

"It is now a matter for the French government but, until the French formally authorise the product it cannot be imported into any member state," a Commission official said. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
